statusLine.command:
input=$(cat)
# `// ""` keeps empty fields in place; `// empty` would collapse the array and shift columns.
out=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '[(.model.display_name // ""), (.context_window.used_percentage // ""), (.context_window.context_window_size // ""), (.effort.level // "")] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null)
model=$(printf '%s' "$out" | cut -f1)
pct=$(printf '%s' "$out" | cut -f2)
size=$(printf '%s' "$out" | cut -f3)
eff=$(printf '%s' "$out" | cut -f4)
[ -z "$model" ] && model=unknown
# Backend: env vars are inherited from the parent Claude Code process.
if [ -n "$CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK" ] && [ "$CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK" != 0 ]; then backend='AWS Bedrock'
elif [ -n "$CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX" ] && [ "$CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX" != 0 ]; then backend='GCP Vertex'
elif [ -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" ]; then backend='API'
else
  # Subscription plan name, e.g. claude_max_20x -> Claude Max 20x. Only this field is read.
  org=$(jq -r '.oauthAccount.organizationType // ""' "${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME}/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$org" in
    '') backend='Claude' ;;
    *) backend=$(printf '%s' "$org" | awk -F_ '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) printf "%s%s", toupper(substr($i,1,1)) substr($i,2), (i<NF?" ":"")}') ;;
  esac
fi
# Context usage against the model's actual window (200k / 256k / 1m).
# A session with no messages yet reports no usage, which is genuinely 0 -- not unknown.
case "$pct" in ''|*[!0-9.]*) pct=0 ;; esac
case "$size" in ''|*[!0-9]*) size='' ;; esac
if [ -n "$size" ] && [ "$size" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
  ctx=$(awk -v p="$pct" -v s="$size" 'BEGIN{
    if (s>=1000000) lim=sprintf("%gm", s/1000000); else lim=sprintf("%gk", s/1000);
    printf "%.0fk/%s (%.0f%%)", (p/100*s)/1000, lim, p }')
else
  # Window size unknown: report the percentage alone rather than guessing a limit.
  ctx=$(awk -v p="$pct" 'BEGIN{printf "%.0f%%", p}')
fi
# No hue: hierarchy comes from weight alone, so the line inherits the terminal theme.
# Bold model, normal-weight fields, dim rules -- only the separators recede.
# Build the separator once so the variable holds real escape bytes, not literal backslashes.
sep=$(printf '\033[2m|\033[0m')
line=$(printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m %s %s' "$model" "$sep" "$backend")
[ -n "$eff" ] && line=$(printf '%s %s %s' "$line" "$sep" "$eff")
printf '%s %s %s\n' "$line" "$sep" "$ctx"
